740560101.text: Whoa, what is this place? Paimon's dizzy from that whole... getting sucked into the book... thing.

740560102.text: I remember this place. I know it. This is the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

740560103.text: It sure does feel like we've been transported to all sorts of strange places under weird circumstances after meeting Ann, huh?

740560105.text: Oh, it's fine. Paimon's not blaming you — she just thinks, uh, that Fontaine really is a magical place!

740560106.text: Still, this is the Narzissenkreuz Ordo... Sounds like an organization the people from the Kingdom would set up in a different country!

740560108.text: The method of entry was pretty interesting too, huh! It was just like that picture book in the Annapausis... We read and read... and then we ended up somewhere else!

740560201.text: #I can probably come up with some nice things, and if I do, I will share them with you first, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

740560202.text: Ah, an Oceanid. It's been a long time since I last saw one of your kind.

740560203.text: Wow! You're back, Caterpillar! How are things? Have you found anything?

740560204.text: The sunshine and the wind feel so good. Everything else seems normal.

740560206.text: Oh, allow Paimon to introduce you two. This is our Oceanid friend, Ann. Ann, this is...

740560207.text: My name is Caterpillar. A pleasure to meet you, Ann.

740560208.text: Likewise, Caterpillar... Huh. Have we met?

740560209.text: My memory is fading, so that is quite possible. If I may be so blunt, what is your relationship with the Red Empress?

740560210.text: The Red Empress? I have no idea who that is, though the name kind of rings a bell.

740560211.text: Then let me try another name... What is your relationship with Lyris?

740560212.text: How do you know that name?

740560213.text: #I went through many adventures with Paimon and Knight {NICKNAME}, only to find that she was merely a character in a story.

740560215.text: Yeah, what's going on? Do you know Lyris, Caterpillar?

740560216.text: Do I? Hmm. Ah. I think I know what's going on.

740560217.text: I'm also a victim of riddles, so I shan't play dumb — I'll tell you everything I know.

740560218.text: Lyris did indeed exist. She was an Oceanid as well, and Narzissenkreuz's name for her within the Ordo was the "Red Empress."

740560219.text: Wait? What? So what happened to her?

740560220.text: I don't know, though I do have a hunch.

740560222.text: I fear this hunch isn't worth bringing up. Besides, I suspect that you've already figured it out, being as smart as you are. Am I wrong?

740560224.text: The first thing you said to me...

740560227.text: What my relation to the Red Empress — or Lyris the Oceanid, is...

740560228.text: In that case, you should visit Mary-Ann in the Annapausis, Caterpillar.

740560229.text: Maybe that will confirm your hunch.

740560231.text: #I won't be troubling you this time, Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon. I'll go with Caterpillar.

740560235.text: Okay, then... We'll see you back here later.

740561001.text: It's fine. Just as "Mary-Ann" dreamed of a past tale, and the tale gave birth to me, I will also rest. In dreams, I might be able to recall more things.

740561002.text: #Perhaps there might be lovely things there, too. If I do recall some, you'll be the first to know, Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

740561003.text: ...Got it. Alright then. Good night, Ann!

740560301.text: Here we are, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo!

740560303.text: I remember this place. I know it. This is indeed the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

740560304.text: Right? We found this place previously as well.

740560305.text: It's just like what happened with the book in the Annapausis...

740560306.text: Hmm, that's right! We read and read... and poof, we showed up in a totally different spot!

740560401.text: That... makes this place something like a secret base, doesn't it? We don't even know where it really is, either...

740560402.text: Are you feeling more calm now, Ann?

740560404.text: ...Or should I drop that title? It was all fake, after all...

740560409.text: #{NICKNAME}'s right, y'know. We've still got a whole bunch of adventures waiting up ahead for us!

740560410.text: Ahem. And... how shall one proceed in peace of mind without a reliable knight at hand, oh lovely maiden?

740560502.text: Right, Paimon's been thinking about that, too. "Mary-Ann" said that your birth was a "beautiful accident." What does that mean?

740560503.text: I think it might simply be that my birth was a coincidence. Just as she said, I am someone she dreamed of — the form she took in the dream.

740560504.text: The things we experienced together were also part of the tale in the dream. If it hadn't been for you, that dream might never have ended...

740560505.text: Or perhaps it might have ended, and I might have disappeared with the "happily ever after." I can't be sure.

740560508.text: This means that "Mary-Ann" is also an Oceanid.

740560512.text: That's what I believe as well. And if that's the case, the things I remembered during our journey should have been her memories... Or so I'd think.

740560513.text: Your knowledge and experience cannot exceed that of the main body.

740560514.text: But when you met her, "you" also became your own entity.

740560515.text: Without a main body to restrict and control you.

740560516.text: So... "become the master of your own fate"... Her last words to me...

740560517.text: Ooh, okay, Paimon gets it now. So, that means that Petit Chou, Al, and the others are creations just like you, right?

740560518.text: I believe that to be the case, yes.

740560519.text: In that case, who was "Mary-Ann," really?

740560520.text: ...This name is very familiar to me.

740560521.text: But I cannot recall why — it's like some part of my body has been frozen.

740560602.text: Alright. I now have a lot of thoughts on the matter — memories and emotions.

740560603.text: When those two children brought me here, it was a lovely place. Everything was new and shiny, just as before.

740560604.text: They were vibrant and excited, like the sunlight shining on the water. They told me that this was our new home, and that they'd brought many new friends. That everything could be like they were before.

740560605.text: But later, they changed. Some things stopped being the same, and the people here changed, too.

740560606.text: Though the Narzissenkreuz Institute of old did not have sunlight, it was very warm. Yet, this place grew ever colder. And then... then...

740560612.text: #I'm sorry, Knight {NICKNAME}... As for the rest, each time I try to recall it, I grow very frightened... and very sad. This is the best I can do for now.

740560613.text: I can sense that many terrible things happened here. I can sense many emotions — rage, terror, but also hope, trust, and admiration.

740560614.text: But all of them make me feel a strange sort of pain, like there are all sorts of shards or impurities embedded in my body. I don't want to... I can't...

740560615.text: Alright, alright! Leave that aside first — there's no need to force it. The more you try to force yourself to remember, the less you'll be able to remember!

740560702.text: I suspect that she was only ever a character in a story. In that tale, we needed to save her and defeat the fell dragon Narcissus.

740560704.text: All stories must have their origins.

740560705.text: Hmm... Speaking of that, Ann, we've heard you mention a place called the Narzissenkreuz Institute before...

740560706.text: #So if we go with {NICKNAME}'s logic, the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom and Adventure Team might have their stories' origin in the Institute and the Ordo, right?

740560901.text: Hmm. It feels like we got our hands on some new clues, but then again not...

740560903.text: I've seen terrifying sights. The primordial waters, the amniotic fluid of the world, and its placenta, devoured to the last. The world fell into utter darkness — never again would the cool spring water flow.

740560904.text: I saw that once. Or perhaps I saw that in the future.

740560905.text: W—Wait a second. Which are you talking about? The past or the future?

740560908.text: Eh? Come on, it's fine. We said we were gonna help you!

740560909.text: No. I truly am happy that the two of you are the first two friends I met since I became "me." For that, you have my thanks.

740560912.text: Gah, why are the two of you being so... formal?

740560913.text: Isn't becoming friends something that just, y'know, happens? When you called out to us and asked for our help, Ann, that was the moment Paimon thought — that's right, you're our friend, and we've gotta help you!

740560915.text: Don't be like that, Ann. If you really wanna thank us, then keep your chin up, and keep those spirits high!

740560916.text: Yes... Yes! You're exactly right, Paimon.

740560917.text: Besides, I have your help — I shouldn't waste it by standing still. I must recall more, and tell you all about it.

740560918.text: Uh, not that you have to push yourself too hard to recall the past...

740561101.text: Ah, an Oceanid. It's been a long time since I last saw one of your kind.

740561102.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, I detect the biological signature of an Oceanid.

740561103.text: Oh, allow Paimon to introduce you... This is our Oceanid friend, Ann. Ann, these two are Caterpillar and...

740561104.text: ...I know — and Seymour, the silly dog.

740561106.text: Relevant data does not exist. I do not believe we have had the honor of meeting, Oceanid Ann.

740561107.text: I've never met you before, either. But I was sure of it the moment I saw you — you must be Seymour.

740561109.text: This must be... No, I don't know, either. This is so strange...

740561110.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

740561111.text: Anyway, let's bring you up to speed...

740561113.text: So, you're searching for Mary-Ann, Seymour...

740561114.text: Agh! No wonder that name felt familiar! The person Seymour mentioned and is looking for also goes by that name!

740561115.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

740561116.text: Hey! Ugh, Paimon's had it with you, you silly dog!

740561117.text: Hmmm... Based on what you said before, they can't be the same Mary-Ann, right? The timing...

740561118.text: I deduce from your statement, then, that you have met someone named Mary-Ann in the past, or have perhaps read or heard about such a person from sources aside from myself?

740561119.text: Well, that was her name, that's for sure. Y'know what, let's do it like this — we can call the Mary-Ann in the Annapausis "Mary-Ann 1," and the one you're looking for, Seymour, can be "Mary-Ann 2"!

740561120.text: Negative. The Ms. Mary-Ann I am searching for is of a higher sequential priority. To prevent confusion, she should be "Mary-Ann 1" instead.

740561121.text: Huh? Why don't you look at it this way, Seymour. 2 is bigger than 1. Doesn't that make it pretty good, too?

740561123.text: Uh, looks like he's stopped functioning again...

740561125.text: Ooh, Paimon didn't think you had any mean bones in you, Ann, but you sure do!

740561126.text: Haha. I don't know why, but I suddenly felt compelled to do that...

740561133.text: Oh, there's no need, but thank you.

740561135.text: Let's get serious now, shall we...

740561136.text: Whoa, Seymour was completely being played by Ann! Anyway, you two have been acquainted now, right?

740561137.text: Yeah. Still, Caterpillar... have we ever met before?

740561148.text: Wait? What? So what happened to her?

740561149.text: I don't know, though I do have a hunch.

740561151.text: #It's just a small guess. But the story about the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom that you two mentioned, {NICKNAME} and Paimon...

740561152.text: Let's just say that I think we can use it as a reference of sorts.

740561153.text: Oh... so no progress for us today, huh?

740561154.text: Still, when we first got here, Paimon couldn't help but notice... The clock here doesn't seem very accurate, does it?

740561156.text: Simply put, it's the Doomsday Clock.

740561158.text: When the clock strikes midnight, the apocalypse will come.

740561159.text: Huh? Doesn't this mean that the end of the world is almost upon us?

740561160.text: Huh, that really does take me back. When I was here before, they thought the apocalypse was still far away, and that though it wouldn't happen in our generation, we should stop it for the sake of the future.

740561161.text: If the clock is accurate, then it is not far off now. Perhaps we shall lay ourselves down to sleep tonight, and the sun shall not rise in the morn. Perhaps the sea shall evaporate tomorrow.

740561162.text: Or perhaps we are already living in the apocalypse, and the good times have long ended.

740561163.text: Hey! Get serious! Will the apocalypse really come?

740561164.text: What we're seeing is a doomsday clock, not doomsday itself. Time is just an invention by man to measure changes.

740561165.text: Narzissenkreuz was the one who used the "world-formula" to calculate the beginning of the end, and built this device.

740561166.text: As such, I cannot answer your question, dear Paimon. Because this is all it is — a clock.

740561169.text: You and Paimon briefly share all that happened with the other three people (though technically speaking, none of them are humans).

740561173.text: I don't know. I'm not sure. It's like water boiling off into gas. I can't see it, and I can't quite grasp it, either.

740561174.text: Oh. Any thoughts or leads, Caterpillar?

740561175.text: Hmm... Can't say that I don't, but I'm still trying to sort some things out, so let's discuss this later.

740561176.text: Oh, I keep forgetting to ask...

740561177.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, I'm very grateful for everything you've done for Lanoire. So, is there anything that I can help you with?

740561178.text: Huh? Do you mean... anything? Just like making a wish?

740561179.text: Haha! It should be something within the scope of my abilities, of course. You did free Lanoire and I from prison, but I'm no Jinn in a bottle.

740561180.text: So, what would your wish be, Paimon?

740561181.text: Hmm, if that's the case, then Mora... No, wait, yummy food...

740561182.text: Argh! Paimon wants lots of things, but...

740561183.text: We've been having lots of fun traveling together, so we don't really need anything special. Instead, Caterpillar, can you help us help Ann and Seymour?

740561185.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Is that alright?

740561188.text: I understand. Then, let us work together.

740561191.text: #Now, I plan to work with Seymour and Ann to see if we can use our experiences and the information available here to figure something new out. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's meet back here later.
